title: Governance review and community engagement framework
subtitle: Also: Smart Cities wind-down, county social services report, Future Ready progress, oath of office, downtown renewal update.
overview: The committee recommended a package of governance changes, including a revised procedural by-law, closed meeting protocol and delegation of authority updates {{vote:m9}}. Two amendments were added along the way. One would require the relevant meeting chair's approval before an information item is added to an agenda {{vote:m8}}. The other says the clerk may suggest, rather than make, administrative edits to motions {{vote:m7}}. It also recommended a new Community Engagement Policy and Charter {{vote:m12}}.

The committee recommended endorsing the Water Services operational plan. Before that, the mayor reported that the closed discussion with staff involved only information and no direction {{vote:m2}}. It also recommended asking the province to amend the municipal oath of office to recognize Indigenous and treaty rights {{vote:m11}}, and it received the Future Ready progress report {{vote:m4}}.

Staff said the Smart Cities Office will close in December 2023 as federal funding ends. The committee recommended encouraging public health to continue food-access work {{vote:m10}}. It also received the County of Wellington's social services report {{vote:m5}} and a downtown renewal update {{vote:m14}}. The update previewed Wyndham Street and bridge options that will go to public consultation. Council will consider all recommendations later.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council endorse the Water Services operational plan, as required under the Ontario Municipal Drinking Water Licensing Program.
The committee received the 2022 progress report and recommended asking local boards and shared services to give annual performance updates alongside strategic plan reporting from June 2024.

The committee recommended approving the amended procedural by-law, closed meeting protocol, CAO and officer-related policies and delegation of authority changes, and directing the clerk and mayor to review the Downtown Guelph advisory group's governance.
The committee recommended amending the procedural by-law to require consultation and approval of the meeting chair before an information item is added to an agenda.
The committee recommended approving the revised Community Engagement Policy and the draft Community Engagement Charter, replacing the 2019 policy and 2015 framework.
The committee received the Smart Cities report and recommended encouraging Wellington-Dufferin-Guelph Public Health to continue food security work and apply lessons from Our Food Future.

The committee recommended asking the provincial minister to amend the municipal declaration of office to recognize Indigenous and treaty rights, and forwarding the resolution to other governments and First Nations.

debate: On the governance review, one councillor questioned a proposed increase in the maximum length of staff-approved agreements from five to ten years. Staff said it was meant to give stability for long-term community lease partners and offered to narrow its scope before final ratification.

On information items, supporters said chair approval prevents items landing on agendas unannounced. Others worried it could block time-sensitive matters. Staff noted that members could still file a notice of motion or ask to suspend the by-law.

Smart Cities delegates asked for a transition plan to keep food and circular-economy work coordinated, saying the program's gains could be lost. Some councillors worried about open-ended funding. The CAO said the pilot and federal money have ended and the work is moving to partners and city teams.

On the Future Ready report, councillors asked how targets are set and where to find them. Staff said targets are simple maintain, increase or decrease measures set by the responsible staff, and agreed to look at adding links to related reports.

In the county social services discussion, councillors pressed on the social housing wait list and on how the city could plan to add housing. County staff said a plan is expected in the fall of 2023 and agreed to bring a fuller picture of local gaps.
